chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah, from Aḥmad/Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq Al-Qazwīni, from Abī Bakkār, who said:

I took some of the dust which is close to the head of the grave of Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.). It was a red-coloured clay. I took it to Imam Riďā (a.s.) to show it to him. He held it in his palm, smelled it, and started to cry, shedding tears. Then he (the Imam (a.s.)) said, “This is the dust of (the grave of) my grandfather.”

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the satisfied one, a title for Imam Ali al-Rida)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Riďā (a.s.) say when shown the dust from the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the Shia tradition of *tabarruk* (seeking blessings) through the physical soil of the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically linking the martyrdom of Imam Husayn with the lineage of Imam Ridha. The Imam’s emotional reaction—smelling the clay and weeping—serves as a profound validation of the site’s sanctity and reinforces the continuity of grief and spiritual connection across generations of Imams. This act transforms the geographical location of Karbala into a tangible medium for divine proximity and remembrance.
